newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bomb blast at Spanish civil guard HQ, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: Bomb blast at Spanish civil guard HQ, no injuries.

text.p: A bomb exploded outside the headquarters of the paramilitary Civil Guard in a northern Spanish town on Saturday, causing property damage but no injuries.
State radio said the bomb went off shortly after 3 a.m. next to Civil Guard headquarters in the small town of Sallent del Gallego in the Aragon region.
The town's mayor, Jose Luiz Sanchez, told reporters he believed it was a "terrorist" attack, a reference to the Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA.
"I suppose the objective was to cause social alarm," Sanchez said. "Any town in this country is prepared for the acts of these terrorists," he added.

The radio said no group had claimed responsibility for the bombing, which shattered windows and damaged other property. ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has frequently targeted the Civil Guard in its 29-year-old campaign for an independent state.
Security forces were searching for the perpetrators around Sallent del Gallego, located in the province of Huesca near the Pyrenees mountains and Spain's border with France.
